newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ANALYSIS-ESTONIA 1996 GDP MAY BE HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSIS-ESTONIA 1996 GDP MAY BE HIGHER.

text.p: Statistics for Estonia's economic growth on Tuesday were lower than in 1995 but analysts said the real figures for last year are probably several percentage points higher than official figures.
The statistics office earlier said that GDP rose four percent last year after 4.3 percent growth in 1995.
But analysts said the figures were not showing all economic activity as the shadow economy was not covered.
They also said various consumption indicators indicated a higher level of growth.
"Estonia's economic growth is at the level of six to seven percent," said Aavo Kokk, board member of key bank Hoiupank.

Heido Vitsur, economic advisor to Prime Minister Mart Siimann, said that indicators such as growing wealth, construction activity, new car sales and retail sales also showed that the economy was growing quicker.
"Indirect indicators show the economy has to liven up more," he told Reuters but said it was impossible to be exact.
The deputy head of the Estonian central bank's macroeconomic department, Teet Rajasalu, said the reason why growth in 1996 was lower than the year before was in the first quarter.
"Growth would have been quicker without frozen ports and export difficulties in the first quarter," he said.
Hoiupank's Kokk said Estonia could maintain its growth due to the country's open economy.
"While we are open, growth will continue. It is easier to make business and quicker to achieve results," he said.
But he noted quicker economic growth had its own dangers as the economy sucked in imports and worsened the trade and current account deficit.
Estonia's current account deficit was 5.3 billion kroons in 1996, up from 2.1 billion kroons a year before.
"There is nothing worring at the moment, as the major part is capital goods, but the amount of consumption goods is increasing," Kokk said.
